title: Measurement of the Included Transaction Allowance and the Overage Charge
content:
Booking transactions made under the Corporate Travel Programmes are counted for each billing period against the tier's included allowance, and every transaction beyond it is charged at the tier's overage rate.

## The window and what is counted in it

The window is the current billing period of the programme, running from the period start date to the period end date carried on that period's subscription line. What is counted within it is the booking transaction fee lines raised on the same programme.

## The charge for a period

The transactions charged are the transactions counted in the period less the tier's included allowance; where the count does not exceed the allowance, the number charged is nothing at all. That number of transactions is multiplied by the tier's published charge for each transaction beyond the allowance.

## How the count is taken

The count is taken on transactions actually completed in the period, so a booking made in one period and cancelled in the next still counts in the period it was made. An unused allowance is never carried into the next period and is never credited back. Transactions on a suspended programme are not counted, because no booking may be made while it is suspended.

## Repeated periods above the allowance

Where a company exceeds its allowance in three consecutive periods it is offered the tier above, and the overage continues to be charged until the move takes effect.

| Basis | Figure |
| --- | --- |
| Consecutive periods above the allowance after which the tier above is offered | 3 |

## How the charge is presented

Overage is charged once for the whole period rather than transaction by transaction, and is stated on the invoice with the count it was measured over.

## Worked illustration, on hypothetical figures

Take a period in which 312 booking transactions are counted on a programme whose tier carries 200 transactions in its subscription and charges 2.00 USD for each transaction beyond them. The transactions charged are 312 less 200, that is 112. One hundred and twelve transactions multiplied by 2.00 USD is 224.00 USD, raised once for that period and stated on the invoice with the count of 312 it was measured over.

Where the same programme completes 180 transactions in a period, the count does not exceed the 200 the tier carries, no overage arises for that period, and the 20 unused transactions are neither carried into the next period nor credited back.
